gbm_population_evidence.quote: Be newly diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme within 4 weeks of open biopsy/resection;

candidate_evidence.quote: MBM-02 (Tempol) is an HIF-1 and HIF-2 inhibitor that is being tested as an addition to standard of care treatment that includes radiotherapy and TMZ.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Increase Survival in Patients With Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM)

role_evidence.quote: Cohort 1 will receive standard of care concomitantly with1000 mg/day of MBM-02.

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational nitroxide antioxidant (Tempol, 4-hydroxy-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl), stated HIF-1/HIF-2 inhibitor; development code MBM-02
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: MBM-02 is an HIF-1 and HIF-2 inhibitor that has shown in animal models to turn back on the apoptosis process (cell death) in cancer.

role_evidence.quote: 2. 6 weeks of radiotherapy and concomitant temozolomide;

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, standard of care for glioblastoma

source_quote.quote: Patients with histone H3 K27M mutation or gliosarcoma;

coder_notes: Active moiety: Tempol has no INN stated in the record; coded 'tempol' (named in record as other name of MBM-02); script may map to development code mbm-02. Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but every patient receives it as standard of care (listed per R9). H3K27M mutation is an exclusion criterion (absence required for entry), coded as eligibility biomarker, not candidate-matched. Exclusion 9 requires sufficient tissue for full molecular profiling, but no specific marker is named. Four sequential dose cohorts (1000/1200/1400 mg/day), none a control. Secondary outcomes on haematological toxicity reduction and radiation necrosis are not target engagement.
